doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Her marriage and her husband
summary: Liston describes two husbands, neither a musician, and her second marriage: loving, on and off, ending amicably, and he cared about her music.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Shall we mention the magic word?
What is that?
Married.
[does not recall the date]. He just died a few months ago.
He was a good guy.
Good and bad and all of that stuff, and I was good and bad and all of that stuff. I guess I was getting ready to leave him a long time, maybe three or four times before I actually left him.
Was he a musician?
No.
That’s right. You said none of them were musicians.
Two husbands. One of them didn’t last no time, because he was on some stuff or something, but my husband that I – I loved him.
That wasn’t hard to say, was it?
No. But you get tired or something. It don’t matter too much.
But you said he cared about you and he’d just call to see how you were.
He cared, and then he didn’t care, and then I left him, and then he started up again.
He started caring, right? He missed you.
Something like that. He used to come and see me in New York there. When I came out here he used to call me up all the time, and I’m sorry he’s gone.
When you had your stroke, did he come to see you?
Yeah. He was nice like that. Both of us just decided not to go through with the marriage no more.
But he didn’t resent your music.
No. He was glad for my music.
Did he come to see you play?
